note_sections.t: Persistent elevation of prostate-specific antigen levels coupled with newly acquired multiparametric MRI findings prompted this clinical encounter.

At 73 years of age, this retired warehouse worker initially entered evaluation in 2022 due to a steady increase in prostate-specific antigen levels. Widowed and currently residing with his partner, he navigates minor mobility constraints with a walking frame. Lower urinary tract symptoms have accompanied him for several years, yielding an IPSS score of 18 that indicates moderate bother; he explicitly denies haematuria or acute urinary retention. Daily activity includes a twenty-minute walk, and his alcohol intake averages seven units weekly. A recent ophthalmology visit addressed routine cataract screening, with no systemic complaints or unexplained weight loss reported. He maintains a 29 pack-year smoking history but ceased consumption in 2018. No regular medications are taken, and known drug allergies are absent.

Digital rectal assessment demonstrates a symmetrically enlarged prostate with a smooth, rubbery consistency and an absence of palpable nodules or asymmetry. General examination remains unremarkable, with stable vital signs and absent lymphadenopathy or abdominal masses. The patient ambulates using a frame per administrative records, yet otherwise appears well-nourished and free of acute distress.

admin: Mobility limitation (frame); ground-floor consult room preferred.
